rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposition of human and jinn deviants follows God's established practice: evildoers have always plotted against prophets, and God gives them respite to carry out their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: established practice in a different way which has been stated earlier in verse 112.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A suppressed imperfect verb in the verse conveys that the plot rebounds on its makers: truth's opponents fatally harm themselves, unaware of their fate; Quraysh will follow the same course.
rows.anchor: Those who oppose the truth do not harm the truth; they in fact fatally harm themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh's leaders asked why God chose Muḥammad rather than leaders from Mecca or Ṭāʾif; Islahi reads this as a political ploy masking conceit and deceiving people who equated worldly prominence with divine standing.
rows.anchor: asked that if God wanted to grant the position of messengerhood to someone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengerhood is God's selective appointment, not an entitlement available to everyone.
rows.anchor: It is in fact a divine appointment which is received only by those who are selected by God for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood and messengerhood are divine blessings reserved for God's chosen people, who are the finest human beings in lofty morals.
rows.anchor: only those people are chosen for these positions are the best human beings standing at the miracle of lofty morals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Working mischief covers all wrongdoing, with particular reference to the arrogance of demanding prophethood; that arrogance brings humiliation and punishment.
rows.anchor: while the words “working mischief” refers to all their wrongdoings, a special reference here is to their arrogance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haraj means a narrow place thick with bushes; following dayyiqan, it intensifies the sense of constriction.
rows.anchor: a narrow place replete with bushes.” Here it occurs after

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb tasadu means to climb an incline with difficulty.
rows.anchor: to climb an incline with difficulty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sama can mean both clouds and the atmosphere.
rows.anchor: means “clouds” it also means “atmosphere.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The real barrier to faith is the filth of disbelief and polytheism on the heart, not the opponents' plots; it makes Islam feel like a steep climb that constricts the chest. God makes such hearts unreceptive, while pure hearts incline to Islam.
rows.anchor: the real thing that stops them from professing faith is the filth of disbelief and polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative pronoun has verbal force, and mustaqiman is an accusative of state; the verse presents Islam as God's straight path, endorsed by human nature and without twists or ups and downs, though unnatural spiritual filth makes it hard to tread.
rows.anchor: meaning of a verb in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has supplied arguments that Islam is the religion of human nature and Abraham's way, but they convince only those willing to be reminded and able to reflect.
rows.anchor: God has furnished all arguments that show that Islam is the religion of human nature as well as the way of Abraham (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The house of peace is the reward of those made receptive to Islam; Islam's adversaries instead face a humiliating abode among the jinn and human companions whose fiendish suggestions they accepted, paralleling the earlier warning to wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: for the adversaries of Islam, there will be the abode of humiliation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these gathers the wrongdoers of 6:123-124 and their human and jinn tempters.
rows.anchor: besides the devils among human beings, the ones among the jinn too will be gathered there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Group of Jinn means Iblis's followers, not the whole jinn community.
rows.anchor: their supreme leader, are the ones implied.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis himself was a jinn who deceived Adam and arrogantly defied the command to prostrate.
rows.anchor: He himself, as is known from the Qur’ ān, belonged to the jinn.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address alludes to Iblis's threats in 17:62 and 7:16-17 that he would mislead Adam's progeny except a few and make most ungrateful; his figurative descendants docilely fulfilled his plan.
rows.anchor: have a very subtle insinuation to the words of the two afore-cited verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual benefit included worship, offerings and vows to jinn deities, changing lawful and unlawful at their behest, and exploitation by soothsayers, magicians, and mediums without reflection.
rows.anchor: these companions from mankind worshipped these deities, made offerings and vows to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs linked jinn with soothsaying, magic, poetic inspiration, every great poet's jinn companion, valleys, travel, settlement, war, peace, and conquest; they even claimed the Prophet had jinn companions.
rows.anchor: the jinn played a very significant role. It was because of the jinn that soothsaying and magic flourished.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human devils' statement is a shameful confession and prelude to pleading for forgiveness, but God interrupts before they finish or can apologize.
rows.anchor: God will interject even before their statement is complete, and without giving them a chance to apologize

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's immediate verdict that Hell is their eternal abode closes the door to apology, excuses, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: so they must not try to present excuses; the doors to apology, excuse and forgiveness now stand closed.

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some exegetes take eternal to mean a long period, since the exception appears to qualify an eternal stay; Islahi rejects this reading.
rows.anchor: exegetes. This is because it shows that apparently “eternal stay” in Hell

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: To avoid the apparent difficulty, some exegetes take ma as man; Islahi rejects this as contrary to Arabic.
rows.anchor: In order to avoid this interpretation, some have regarded

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception does not mean Hell ends: once punishment begins, hope, intercession, pleading, repentance, reform, and freedom of will are gone; only God's will remains, whose secrets He alone knows.
rows.anchor: the exception is not meant to express the fact that the time of stay in Hell will end one day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is as far as the Qur'an's words can be taken; further inferences should be judged on their own merits, not attributed to the Qur'an, and eternity is a divine mystery whose disclosed limits people should accept.
rows.anchor: It is not right to regard it to be the purport of the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 6:129 explains 6:128; the words wilaya and tawliya mean putting someone in charge or control of another.
rows.anchor: means to make someone in charge and in control of someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human misdeeds, not inherent satanic authority, explain why devils control so many: people abandon God's guidance for desire and religious innovations, become Satan's followers, and thereby incur God's established law.
rows.anchor: it is not because these devils have any authority over human beings; the misdeeds of these human beings are the reason for it.
